body:
`uv pip compile` selects `backports-strenum==1.3.1` for Python 3.12.6 although that release declares `Requires-Python: >=3.8.6,<3.11`. Installing the result succeeds, but `uv pip check` then reports the incompatibility.

Environment: macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.6, `uv 0.12.18 (01cb90c1a 2026-09-22 aarch64-apple-darwin)`.

Reproducer (requirements.txt contains only `ai-edge-litert==2.3.0`):

```sh
uv pip compile requirements.txt --python-version 3.12.6
```

The result contains:

```text
ai-edge-litert==2.3.0
backports-strenum==1.3.1
    # via ai-edge-litert
```

LiteRT's installed metadata requires `backports.strenum` without a marker. Both PyPI JSON and installed wheel metadata for 1.3.1 declare the Python upper bound. The error from `uv pip check` is:

```text
The package `backports-strenum` requires Python >=3.8.6, <3.11, but `3.12.6` is installed
```

Expected: select a compatible release (1.2.8 declares `>=3.8.6,<4.0.0`) or fail resolution. An explicit `backports.strenum<1.3` constraint selects 1.2.8 and restores a clean dependency check. This was reproduced using a dedicated uv cache during optional model-runtime provisioning.

Metadata references: https://pypi.org/pypi/backports.strenum/1.3.1/json and https://pypi.org/pypi/backports.strenum/1.2.8/json .
title: pip compile selects backports-strenum with incompatible Requires-Python for Python 3.12
